transcript.label: Transcript turn 20 · “Will you be doing all of this for me? What if I don’t have such systems?”

text: Most of it is ours. A small part is not, and it is better said now.
bullets: We bring the recording. Voice notes on rounds, with our own recorder. Prescriptions read at OPD. Each admission step timed as it happens.
Two things have to be there already. Read access to what holds admissions, discharges, tests and charges. And one report on your billing system.
If almost nothing is digital, this is a different project, not a slower one. The recording layer gets much bigger.

chat.note: We bring the recording. You bring the access.

sheets.title: Voice notes on rounds
sheets.text: The doctor speaks on the round they already do. Our recorder and our transcription turn it into a note. Nobody types it again.
sheets.entry: Do your doctors record notes on rounds today?

sheets.title: Prescriptions read at OPD
sheets.text: The advice to admit is read from the prescription as the doctor writes it. It is not a form for somebody to fill in.

sheets.title: Admission steps timed

sheets.title: Read access
sheets.text: We read whatever holds admissions, discharges, tests and charges today. We write nothing back.

sheets.title: One billing report
sheets.text: Your billing system holds the time each bill closes and opens. One report joins them against the same bed.
